title: Kelly Clarkson Confirms Singing ‘Golden’ on Final Talk Show Was Hella Hard: ‘It Took Me Forever to Place it to Where I Didn’t Sound Like a Dying Cat!’
summary: The singer also reminisced about her sweet interaction with late country icon Dolly Parton on Monday night's (Sept. 21) Late Night With Seth Meyers.
body: Kelly Clarkson is used to making the vocally impossible look easy, but even she had to admit that singing the KPop Demon Hunters Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 smash “Golden” on the final episode of her syndicated Kelly Clarkson Show was, like, very, very hard. Clarkson, debuting a new shoulder-length bob haircut in a visit to Late Night With Seth Meyers on Monday night (Sept. 21), explained that “Golden” was the most requested Kellyoke track during the syndicated talk show’s seven-year run, so she decided to save it for the very last episode. “But that is … that song is basically humans against AI,” she laughed, as Meyers described realizing in real time watching her performance just how complicated a song it is to sing. “I don’t really understand the inner workings of music, but I was like, ‘Oh, I think this is very hard,'” Meyers recalled. title: The Retroid Pocket Duo Lite Plus might be the Goldilocks dual-screen handheld
summary: The Pocket Duo Lite Plus might strike the best balance between performance, features, and price.
body: Credit: Retroid TL;DR Retroid has announced the Pocket Duo Lite Plus dual-screen handheld. This model is similar to the Pocket Duo Lite but offers the Pocket Duo’s chipset and base RAM/storage. The Pocket Duo Lite Plus has a discounted launch price of $199. Retroid announced the Retroid Pocket Duo and Pocket Duo Lite last week, the latest entry in the increasingly crowded dual-screen handheld space. The standard Pocket Duo is the more upmarket option, while the Lite version makes a few compromises for the price. Does neither option work for you? Then Retroid has now revealed the Pocket Duo Lite Plus. The Retroid Pocket Duo Lite Plus is effectively a middle ground between the Pocket Duo and Pocket Duo Lite. Perhaps the most notable change is the switch from the Lite’s QCS6125 chipset to the standard model’s Q-7790 processor. In other words, you’re effectively going from a low-end Snapdragon 665 chip to a more modern Snapdragon 7 Gen 4.
